label: STOPP D13
title: Anticholinergic medicine for antipsychotic movement effects
statement: Anticholinergic/antimuscarinic drugs (biperiden, orphenadrine, procyclidine, trihexyphenidyl) to treat extra-pyramidal side-effects of antipsychotic medications (risk of anticholinergic toxicity).

source.document: O'Mahony D, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632, Appendix 1 (corrected supplementary file; NHS Somerset copy used for text, sentence-identical to the earlier parse)

plain_summary: An anticholinergic medicine given to treat movement side effects of an antipsychotic can cause anticholinergic toxicity, such as confusion, dry mouth and urine retention.

medicine_groups.name: Anticholinergic medicines for movement side effects
medicine_groups.note: Benzhexol is the former name for trihexyphenidyl and also counts. Norflex, Norgesic and historical Disipal identify orphenadrine. Norgesic also contains paracetamol. The brand alone does not establish why it was taken. Generic packs showing an ingredient with a sponsor name count. Benztropine (Cogentin) is not named in the statement and is not in this group.

medicine_groups.name: Antipsychotic medicines
medicine_groups.note: These are the medicines whose movement side effects the group A medicines are used to treat. Quetiapine and clozapine are included here because this criterion covers any antipsychotic. Prochlorperazine and metoclopramide, used for nausea, are not in this group. Long-acting injections and asenapine sublingual wafers count. Generic packs showing an ingredient with a sponsor name count. Match a salt and its base as one supply. Clopixol Acuphase is the acetate injection for acute treatment. Use its own documented interval. Clopixol Depot is the decanoate maintenance injection.

rule_for_models: If age is unknown and the other evidence supports a finding, report at most a possible finding and ask for the person's age. For a person aged 65 or older, count the days between a Group A anticholinergic supply and a Group B antipsychotic supply and treat the timing condition as met if the gap is 60 days or less or their supply periods overlap. The 60-day date test works even if directions are unclear. For a longer gap, use quantity and directions for tablets or the recorded administration date and prescribed interval for an injection. A documented schedule that links a supply to its injection date can also establish coverage. Only for a pair more than 60 days apart whose periods could still overlap, ask for 'Overlap of the anticholinergic and antipsychotic treatment periods' if the dose, injection date or interval leaves the timing uncertain. Identify the two medicines and supply dates, then check the dated dosing or administration records for that pair. Documented overlap meets the timing condition. If overlap is missing, Not known or cannot be linked to that pair, report at most a possible finding naming that fact, unless another reason rules out the finding. Assess each pair separately. If the supplies are more than 60 days apart and their treatment periods are known to be separate, give no finding even if the indication is missing. Cite both supplies and the indication line when it links the anticholinergic to treatment of a movement side effect of the antipsychotic. If the reason is missing or recorded as Not known, cite both qualifying supplies and report a possible finding that names the missing reason, but report no finding if the only recorded reason is another use.
cannot_be_seen: Why the anticholinergic medicine was prescribed (it is also used for Parkinson's disease), whether the person has movement side effects, and medicines supplied by a hospital or another pharmacy.
ask_the_gp: Whether the anticholinergic medicine is still needed, and whether a change to the antipsychotic or its dose would remove the movement effects.

needs_facts.meets: The record links the Group A medicine to treatment of a movement side effect of the antipsychotic.

options.words: This anticholinergic treated movement side effects caused by the antipsychotic under review
It was used solely for another reason

needs_facts.what: Overlap of the anticholinergic and antipsychotic treatment periods
needs_facts.meets: For the two supplies under review, dated dosing or injection records establish that their treatment periods overlapped.

options.words: Dated records show that these two treatment periods overlapped
Dated records show that these two treatment periods were separate
